# A maximum half-depth extraction can have an unused interior fiber

This exact example prevents an unconditional inference from the new
base-moment correction to a paid bulge. It concerns n=d=1 and beta=gamma_1
=1/2. Its optimum is ABOVE the desired half-mass threshold, so it does not
refute a below-threshold-specific mechanism or OC.

Let

    C=conv{(0,0),(3,0),(3,3),(2,10),(0,2)}.

Its integer fibers are [0,2],[0,6],[0,10],[0,3] at bases0,1,2,3,
respectively, and its mixed mass is M=21. The complete exact reflection
calculation in
`candidate 1176a6cc970482b9`
proves

    max_(integer-base y in C) |C intersect (2y-C) intersect Lambda|=12,

with unique maximizing center (2,3). In particular that result optimizes
over ALL continuous center locations in each integer fiber, not just the
ordinary fiber midpoints.

Define D by its three positive fibers

    D_1=[3,6],   D_2=[0,6],   D_3=[0,3],

and take their convex hull. The lower endpoints 3,0,0 are convex and the
upper endpoints 6,6,3 are concave. Thus these are its exact integer fibers,
and D subset C. It is centrally symmetric about (2,3), has mass12, and
has true centroid (2,3). Every closed through-center cap has at least6
mass, so D is feasible at beta=1/2.

It is a GLOBAL maximum among all actual convex half-depth extractions.
Indeed the independently proved interval half-depth rigidity theorem
`candidate f9fd3b8e5ea799fa`
implies that every such extraction has centrally symmetric positive
mixed measure about its true integer-base centroid. Its mass is bounded
by the original body's reflection retention there, and hence by12.
This argument is about local HALF-depth; no conjectural local-gamma
theorem is used.

The base2 is in ri(conv{1,2,3}), yet D_2=[0,6] strictly misses part of
C_2=[0,10]. Therefore a genuine maximum extraction may have unused
source at an interior integer base. Although the exponential correction
can restore the base moment of a small bulge with net mass gain, such a
corrected body CANNOT remain half-deep: that would contradict the exact
optimal mass12.

The unpaid active cap can also be seen directly for the simplest bulge.
Raise only the upper endpoint of D_2 from6 to6+t, 0<t<=1. These remain
compatible fibers and lie in C. The added mass is t at base2, so no base
correction is even necessary. Its true continuous centroid is

    c_t=3+(3t+t^2/2)/(12+t).

The through-new-centroid cap

    x+(z-2)>=c_t

cuts all three fibers properly on this t interval. Its mass is

    (6-c_t-1)+(6+t-c_t)+(3-c_t+1)
      =15+t-3c_t.

Subtracting half the new total mass gives EXACTLY

    15+t-3c_t-(12+t)/2 = -t(3+t)/(12+t)<0.          (1)

The old cap is active at t=0, and its first-order deficit is -t/4.
In the active influence function from the exponential-correction note,
this is the identity 1-1/2-(3/12)*3=-1/4: the added law is at continuous
margin3, and the old section count is3.

The optimum12 is strictly larger than M/2=21/2. This example closes only
an unconditional paid-interior-bulge assertion, not a version using an
additional hypothetical below-threshold maximum.
